correctness.rationale: For the first family \(1\le q\le2\), the only nonunit distance is the antipodal distance \(q\), so the metric axioms hold and Kalenda's Proposition 8.2 gives the matching \(q\)-Schur upper bound. The alternating evaluation sequence has tail diameter \(q\). A unit Lipschitz function can have an antipodal value gap exceeding 1 on at most one pair; after deleting it the scalar tail range is at most 1, and an explicit sign function attains 1. Hence \(\delta=1\) and the optimal constant is at least \(q\). For the second family \(2\le q\le3\), the distances \(1,2,q\) satisfy the triangle inequalities. Antipodal molecules have norm \(q\), while any unit Lipschitz function has all but at most two antipodal differences in \([-1,1]\); therefore every weak-star cluster point has norm at most 1. Kalenda's Proposition 5.1 then excludes every constant below \(q\), and Proposition 8.2 supplies the upper bound. The universal lower bound 1 and the 2026 universal 3-Schur theorem complete the exact spectrum \([1,3]\).
